comparisons.peer_summary: Fair value hedges protect against interest rate or foreign exchange volatility in assets and liabilities, with derivative fair value changes recorded in earnings alongside the hedged item's changes. If terminated, previous adjustments to the hedged item's carrying value are amortized to earnings over the asset or liability's remaining life for interest-bearing items.
comparisons.comparison: MS and BAC both disclose that for qualifying fair value hedges, the change in fair value of the derivative and the hedged item are recognized in earnings. Both firms report these changes in the same income statement line item, consistent with MS's description of recognizing them as a component of Interest income (expense).

sentences.text: For qualifying fair value hedges of benchmark interest rates, the change in the fair value of the derivative, offset by the change in the fair value attributable to the change in the benchmark interest rate risk of the hedged asset (liability), is recognized in earnings each period as a component of Interest income (expense).

Changes in the fair value of derivatives designated as fair value hedges are recorded in earnings, together and in the same income statement line item with changes in the fair value of the related hedged item.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Presentation of Fair Value Hedges on Interest Rate Risk
comparisons.peer_summary: For qualifying fair value hedges of interest rate risk, changes in the fair value of the derivative and the hedged item are presented within Interest income or Interest expense, depending on whether the hedged item is an asset or a liability.
comparisons.comparison: MS and C both confirm that for qualifying fair value hedges of interest rate risk, the changes in fair value of the derivative and hedged item are recognized in earnings within Interest income or Interest expense. Both disclosures align on the income statement line item for this recognition.

sentences.text: For qualifying fair value hedges of benchmark interest rates, the change in the fair value of the derivative, offset by the change in the fair value attributable to the change in the benchmark interest rate risk of the hedged asset (liability), is recognized in earnings each period as a component of Interest income (expense).

For qualifying fair value hedges of interest rate risk, the changes in the fair value of the derivative and the change in the fair value of the hedged item attributable to the hedged risk are presented within Interest income or Interest expense based on whether the hedged item is an asset or a liability.

comparisons.peer_summary: Effectiveness is evaluated at inception and ongoing on retrospective and prospective bases using quantitative correlation measures, with consistent methodologies applied across similar hedges and potential exclusions for unrelated value changes and time value.
comparisons.comparison: MS uses regression analysis for effectiveness assessment, while C uses quantitative measures of correlation evaluated on a prospective and retrospective basis. Both firms evaluate effectiveness at inception and on an ongoing basis, reflecting a similar methodology for assessing hedge performance, though MS specifies regression while C specifies correlation measures.

sentences.text: The Firm uses regression analysis to perform an ongoing prospective and retrospective assessment of the effectiveness of these hedging relationships.

The effectiveness of these hedging relationships is evaluated at hedge inception and on an ongoing basis both on a retrospective and prospective basis, typically using quantitative measures of correlation.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm uses regression analysis to assess hedge effectiveness, requiring a coefficient of determination of 80% or greater and a slope between 80% and 125% for an interest rate swap to be considered highly effective.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS explicitly state they use regression analysis to assess hedge effectiveness for interest rate risk. However, GS provides specific quantitative thresholds for effectiveness (coefficient of determination >= 80% and slope between 80%-125%), whereas MS describes the method generally without citing specific statistical benchmarks.

sentences.text: The Firm uses regression analysis to perform an ongoing prospective and retrospective assessment of the effectiveness of these hedging relationships.

The firm applies a statistical method that utilizes regression analysis when assessing the effectiveness of these hedging relationships in achieving offsetting changes in the fair values of the hedging instrument and the risk being hedged (i.e., interest rate risk).

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment for interest rate fair value hedges
comparisons.peer_summary: For qualifying interest rate fair value hedges, gains or losses on derivatives and the hedging adjustment to the carrying value of hedged items are included in interest income/expense, with remaining differences amortized using the effective interest method upon de-designation.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose that for qualifying fair value hedges of interest rate risk, the changes in fair value of the derivative and the hedged item are recognized in earnings as a component of interest income or expense. Both firms follow the same core accounting treatment for these hedges.

sentences.text: For qualifying fair value hedges of benchmark interest rates, the change in the fair value of the derivative, offset by the change in the fair value attributable to the change in the benchmark interest rate risk of the hedged asset (liability), is recognized in earnings each period as a component of Interest income (expense).
For qualifying interest rate fair value hedges, gains or losses on derivatives are included in interest income/expense.

The change in fair value of the hedged items attributable to the risk being hedged is reported as an adjustment to its carrying value (hedging adjustment) and is also included in interest income/expense.
